title: Autodetect compilation strategy and staged pin workflow for MoE / GQA / MHA models
creator: Ariadne Chen
description:
Objective: implement an automated onboarding flow that detects model attention architecture (standard MHA, grouped-query attention/GQA, and mixture-of-experts/MoE) and selects a tailored compilation strategy plus a staged pin/publish lifecycle for performance profiles.

Scope: changes touch the model-onboarder service, compile profiles database, runtime kernel selector, and Console rollout UI. The system should: 
- Autodetect attention variant at import time using lightweight bytecode/graph heuristics and a short sample-run signature.
- Generate a prioritized compile strategy set (microkernel choices, quantization-safe paths, KV-caching expectations) per architecture.
- Run a constrained compile+benchmark sandbox (on CI pool) against representative sequence-length buckets and batch shapes to produce candidate profiles.
- Publish profiles as: candidate -> canary (small percentage traffic) -> pinned. Each stage must record performance delta vs baseline and pass SLO/cost gates.
- Provide a manual override and rollback in Console and an API for automation (pin/unpin/promote).

Success criteria: 
- New onboarding flow correctly identifies architecture in >=98% of sampled models in our benchmark suite.
- Candidate-to-pinned promotions record <=5% perf regression risk (measured by distributional latency P95 and token cost).
- Console exposes per-profile telemetry and a one-click rollback.

Non-goals: automated kernel authoring or deep model surgery. We will rely on existing compiler transforms and kernel implementations; this effort coordinates selection and staged promotion, not new kernel research.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ariadne Chen: Kickoff meeting notes attached. We agreed on a three-stage publish flow and the need for a sandbox compile cluster (small GPU fleet) to run microbenchmarks. Action items: proto signature heuristics (Mateo), Console UX draft (Rina), telemetry schema (Jordan).

2025-02-20 - Mateo Rivera: Initial heuristics implemented in model-onboarder: detects GQA by grouped attention pattern and MoE by expert linear layers signature. Found 3 false-positives on opt-family; added a second-pass sample inference to validate. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboarder/pull/212

2025-02-26 - Jordan Patel: Telemetry schema v1 landed: profile_id, model_id, arch_tag, seq_bucket, batch_shape, compile_flags, bench_p50,p95,p99,token_cost_usd. Hooked into metrics pipeline with limited retention (30d) for canary analysis. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/87

2025-02-28 - Rina Sato (Design): Console mockups uploaded: two views (Profile matrix and Promotion history). Added a one-click rollback and promoted-by column. Figma: https://redwood.design/f/console-profiles-54821

2025-03-03 - Mateo Rivera: Sandbox compile runner implemented; running nightly benchmark jobs on the ci-compile pool. Observed that MoE profiles need expert-aware KV cache sizing to avoid memory blowups on long seqs. Filed follow-up ENG-54822 for memory tuning in runtime.

2025-03-04 - Security (Priya Singh): Requested KMS alignment for storing signed profiles and an audit trail for promotions. Security review opened; requires HSM key wrap for production pinned profiles.
notes: Trade-offs considered: conservative default to fall back to MHA-compatible kernels when detection confidence < 0.7 to avoid regressions vs. aggressive specialization that yields better throughput but higher risk.
Rollout plan: enable candidate profiles for internal tenants first, then open canary to 5% of production traffic for 48 hours with automatic rollback on SLO breaches.
Monitoring: compare pinned profile performance to baseline using a metric set (p95 latency, token-cost, headroom for throughput). Automated alerts on >7% p95 regression or >10% cost increase.
